BEFORE THE STATE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS

PUCT Docket No. 59475

POST-HEARING BRIEF OF INTERVENORS

Intervenors: Randy Eldridge, Randy & Tina Eldridge, and Zymac Group Ltd.
Intervenor Filing Date: April 14, 2026 (Item No. 2904)

Link G73

      Zymac Group Ltd. Tracts: 5330, 5331

      Randy & Tina Eldridge Tracts: 5327, 5332

      Randy Eldridge Tract: 5324

Intervenor Randy Eldridge, on behalf of Randy Eldridge, Randy & Tina Eldridge, and Zymac
Group Ltd., respectfully submits this Post-Hearing Brief regarding the proposed Link G73
route.

I. Applicant Testimony
 During the evidentiary hearing, Applicants testiﬁed that:

a. Their routing analysis considered the presence of archaeological sites; and

b. Their routing analysis considered the presence of occupied habitable structures.

II. Conditions Existing on Intervenors' Property

Applicants have proposed the Link G73 route for the construction of 765-kV transmission
lines and associated transmission structures across ﬁve tracts owned by the Intervenors.
These tracts contain both documented archaeological resources and occupied habitable
structure, including:

A. Recorded Archaeological Sites

The following archaeological sites have been documented through the Texas Historical
Commission Landowner Assistance Program:

   1. Bell County Field ID TRE-1 – Trinomial 41BL1467

   2. Bell County Field ID TRE-2 – Trinomial 41BL1468

   3. Bell County Field ID TRE-3 – Trinomial 41BL1469



B. Occupied Habitable Structure

The property contains a permanent home occupied residents and it is not a mobile or RV
type home.

III. Requested Route Modiﬁcation

Throughout their testimony and submitted exhibits, Intervenors have consistently
requested that the Link G73 alignment be shifted farther north.

The proposed northern adjustment would provide a straighter alignment across a portion of
Intervenors' property. Applicants have grouped this portion of the property with neighboring
land owned by an unrelated property owner, despite the properties having no common
ownership or relationship.

The alternative route would also utilize properties whose owners did not ﬁle protests,
interventions, or comments regarding the project. Unlike Intervenors' property, the
alternate route property has been for sale and are not used for agricultural operations,
archaeological preservation, water well protection, hay production, or the preservation of
long-held family land.
 IV. Beneﬁts of the Alternative Alignment

The alternative northern route would:

   1. Eliminate the unnecessary zig-zag conﬁguration currently proposed;

   2. Reduce the number of transmission structures required;

   3. Minimize impacts to documented archaeological resources;

   4. Reduce impacts to occupied residential property;

   5. Better protect agricultural operations and water resources;

   6. Accomplish the Applicants' transmission objectives in a more reasonable and
      equitable manner; and

   7. Result in less overall damage to a ected landowners.




V. Conclusion

For the foregoing reasons, Intervenors respectfully request that the Applicants reconsider
the currently proposed Link G73 alignment and give serious consideration to the alternative
route described in the testimony and exhibits submitted in this proceeding.

Respectfully submitted,



Randy Eldridge



CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

parties of record in PUCT Docket No. 59475 through the Public Utility Commission of Texas
ﬁling system on this 19th day of June, 2026.



Randy Eldridge
